title: Volterra Kernels and the Torus — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Volterra Kernels and the Torus's rich face, its first round at Sketch tier: two made pieces, each walking up to a test of its section's claim — where the synth and the effect are one reader and where they are not, and what the diagonal of a kernel really throws away — with the fingerprint of the words each was laid against, and the findings the text has not yet taken, held as offers. I grow when the generalized slice processor gets built and has something to play; I never hold the entry's words.

offers.what: "Preserves harmonic generation but discards intermodulation" does not hold. Two tones (300 and 450 Hz, 0.45 each) through the second-order kernel on its diagonal, x(t)²: both harmonics at −19.89 dB, the sum and the difference products at −13.87 dB, 6.02 dB above them (the piece's worklet, headless, 48 and 44.1 kHz). The diagonal keeps intermodulation at full strength. What it gives up is the freedom to weight a product by the pair that made it: on the diagonal H₂(f₁, f₂) = G(f₁ + f₂), so a product is weighted only by where it lands. Off it, at D = 3.33 ms (x(t)·x(t − D)), the sum product falls below −96 dB and stays there through a 150 Hz glide, harmonics unchanged; a notch after the diagonal, tuned to the sum at 750 Hz, lets it back to −14.7 dB at +75 Hz and takes the 2f₁ harmonic to −97.6 dB instead. Proposed: "…which preserves harmonic generation and intermodulation alike, but weights every product only by the frequency it lands on: what it discards is memory across lags, the products x(t − τ₁)·x(t − τ₂) with τ₁ ≠ τ₂ that let a kernel shape an intermodulation product apart from the harmonics." The same clause recurs in Forward Vectors ("what intermodulation structure it carries that a Hammerstein diagonal discards") and is cited as the load-bearing content in Artifact; both would follow. The page's own gloss in What a Volterra kernel is, "intermodulation between pairs of past samples", should change with it, to "products of pairs of past samples": on that private meaning (cross-lag products) the sentence is true, on the audio meaning (sum and difference tones) it is false, and left alone the gloss will seem to back the old sentence. The off-diagonal null at D = 3.33 ms is half a period of the 150 Hz difference frequency, D = 1/(2Δf), not anything of the sum; the difference product vanishes there too only because 750 Hz × 3.33 ms is 2.5 cycles. Challenger confirmed from the series.

A diagonal-only Volterra series gives each order its own filter, g₁, g₂, g₃…; that is a parallel (polynomial) Hammerstein, a bank of power branches each with its filter. A single Hammerstein, one static curve then one filter, is the special case where every order shares one filter. Proposed: "equivalent to a (parallel) Hammerstein structure".

The page names the input-read three ways: the opening paragraph indexes the field "with products of the input's own past", the Volterra definition weights products by a field indexed by lags, and the Processing bullet indexes the field by the delayed values themselves, (x(t − τ₁), x(t − τ₂), …). The bullet's reading is a Volterra system, but its kernel is not the field: expand the field as a polynomial in the two amplitudes and its coefficients become kernel weights at the lags 0 and D. Measured on the piece: the Chebyshev field read by a plucked riff matches Σ c_jk·T_j(x(t))·T_k(x(t − D)) within 1.4 × 10⁻⁴ (peak 0.90; the gap is the 256-point table's interpolation). Proposed: in the opening, "by indexing it with the input's own past values"; after the bullets, "Read this way the field is not itself the kernel. Its Chebyshev coefficients are the synth's partial table; the kernel's weights at those lags are the same grid re-expanded as plain powers (T₂ = 2x² − 1 feeds orders 0 and 2), so one grid determines both without being the same numbers." Not played by either piece, and worth the next round: a lag reader, the table used as h₂ itself (y = Σ T[i, j]·x(t − i)·x(t − j)), where the field literally is the kernel; the challenger found its H₂ on the grid equals L² times the synth's 2D Fourier partials (one entry checked, −0.003631 + 0.013348j both sides), the page's "same object" word for word.

An addition the toggle earned. The two readers meet exactly in one place: a full-scale sine into the effect is the synth scanning at 1 : 1 with its second phasor lagging f·D of a turn. Effect − synth on the a·b, tanh and Chebyshev fields: −267 to −297 dB on the piece's engine (D = 0, 17, 96, 240 samples, 48 and 44.1 kHz), −255 to −319 dB in the challenger's independent recompute on continuous fields: machine precision. They part when the field is not the same mirrored across each axis (the (3,2) ridge: +2.2 dB) or the sine is below full scale (0.9: −9.6 dB; 0.7: −3.4 dB). The condition is mirroring, a field that is a function of the two amplitudes alone, not that it is a polynomial: tanh passes. An amplitude names a phase only up to its sign, so under any single-valued amplitude map the effect goes there and back and never winds round the torus; that it reaches only a quarter belongs to the inverse-cosine map the piece chose (a linear map would sweep a whole axis). Proposed, after the first bullet: "They meet at one point: a full-scale sine into the effect is the synth at 1 : 1, on any field that looks the same mirrored across both axes. Elsewhere the effect reads the field through amplitude, which goes there and back and never winds, so the torus the synth lives on is invisible to it."

"Ring modulation as the simplest input-read special case (the bilinear slice)": a ring modulator as built, input times a carrier, reads one axis by the input and the other by a phasor, the halfway reading between synth and effect. Measured on the piece's half reader, a·b field, 220 Hz in, 110 Hz carrier: 110 and 330 Hz at 0.4500 each, 220 Hz at 10⁻¹⁶. The pure input-read bilinear slice is the input times its own past, x(t)·x(t − D), which is the off-diagonal kernel of the next section's piece. Proposed: "ring modulation as the hinge between the two (the bilinear field, one axis read by the input and the other by a phasor); read by the input alone, the bilinear slice is the input times its own past". This holds for a ring modulator with its own carrier oscillator, the common build. A ring modulator of two external signals is a two-input cross-kernel, input-read on both axes by different signals, and fits the page's single-input series no better (challenger).

verdicts.why: A real test that came out against the text: on the diagonal intermodulation is 6.02 dB over the harmonics (recomputed from the series, H₂ = G(f₁+f₂)), carried as offer 1, not written in. Walks harmonics, intermodulation and memory each alone before the two-tone test; note the glide hint (the difference product nulls again at +150 Hz).

pieces.title: the diagonal and off it
pieces.caption: A static curve, then two signals multiplied, then a sine times its own past, then the test: two tones into the second-order kernel, read on its diagonal and off it, with what each slice keeps predicted and measured. On the diagonal intermodulation comes out 6 dB above the harmonics. One step off, at D = 3.33 ms, half a period of the 150 Hz difference between the tones, the sum product is gone and stays gone through a glide that keeps that spacing; the difference product vanishes there too, by coincidence (750 Hz × 3.33 ms = 2.5 cycles). Checked headless on the piece's own worklet: Rich face checks/check-pieces.mjs.
pieces.near: The single most clarifying technical result

verdicts.why: Builds the toggle the section asks for, then tests whether the two readers are one; the ridge and the lowered level show it can fail (+2.2, −9.6, −3.4 dB; mirrored fields at machine precision, recomputed). Fix in passing: the input-step hint calls the diagonal section "the next section" (it comes before) and reuses "the two readers" for u and v.

pieces.title: one field, two readers
pieces.caption: The one-field-two-modes surface: a stored table read by your hand, by two phasors, by a plucked riff and its own past, then one button that flips scan, half and input. Last, the test: a full-scale sine into the effect against the synth at 1 : 1, and the meter on their difference. They are one signal on a field that looks the same mirrored; on the ridge, or below full scale, they come apart. Checked headless on the piece's own worklet: Rich face checks/check-pieces.mjs.
